analysis.title: Global Credit Outlook 2027: The race to the next trillion
key_insights: HSBC's base case for 2027 is that the AI credit cycle continues but the growth rate of borrowing moderates. IG spreads stay in the recent 80-100bp range. The focus shifts from the volume of debt to capex payoffs, repayment cashflows and financing structures.

Three scenarios frame the year. Base case: borrowing continues and spreads stay at about 80-100bp. Pause: an external shock widens IG spreads up to 120bp and then they recover, which HSBC says could be modestly credit-positive. Halt: markets lose confidence in AI returns, spreads widen beyond 120bp and leveraged AI pure plays such as neoclouds are most exposed.

Strategy positions for the base case, prepares for the pause and guards against the halt. HSBC favours EUR and GCC spread beta, front-end BBs, T2s and corporate hybrids over spread duration, and contractual-cashflow AI exposure over exposure to the AI endgame.

Total return forecasts for Nov 2026 to Nov 2027: USD IG 8.3%, EUR IG 6.2%, GBP IG 9.5%, USD HY 9.6%, EUR HY 8.4%, GCC 8.6%, Asia 8.1%. Year-end 2027 spread forecasts: USD IG 85bp, EUR IG 90bp, GBP IG 95bp, USD HY 300bp, EUR HY 300bp, GCC 105bp, Asia 85bp.

Stance changes: US HY goes to Neutral from mildly bearish. EUR IG and EUR HY go to mildly bullish from neutral. USD IG stays Neutral, GBP stays Neutral, GCC stays mildly bullish and Asia stays Neutral.

The repricing from competition for capital has come through real yields, not spreads. Breakevens, term premia and swap spreads have been mostly stable, which HSBC reads as the market rethinking where the short-term r-star sits.

Demand should absorb supply. US IG gross issuance is forecast at USD1,980bn (+8%), supported by foreign inflows from Asian and European investors and by coupon reinvestment, since the average US IG coupon is above 4.5%. EUR demand may start 2027 tepid and improve as Bund yields ease and insurer balance sheet constraints loosen.

Hyperscalers can borrow a further USD600bn before hitting a theoretical 2% issuer concentration limit, so the pace of issuance, not the stock of debt, is the binding constraint. That constraint is tighter in CHF and GBP, where hyperscalers are over half of industrial bond supply in 2026.

Off-balance-sheet financing is growing quickly. HSBC estimates USD400-500bn of GPU-backed and datacentre debt, up from under USD100bn a year ago. Rating agencies already count these leases in hyperscaler leverage. Datacentre bonds often offer a 100-200bp spread uplift over the tenant hyperscaler, with duration typically under 5 years.

HSBC prefers datacentre bonds with strong hyperscaler leases, debt amortising within the lease term and limited construction risk. Oracle declared force majeure on Project Jupiter and both Oracle bonds and the Red Chiles construction loan spreads widened. Around a quarter of rated datacentre SPV bonds have elevated force-majeure risk.

AI complex interdependencies are dense. HSBC mapped 179 relationships (leases, equity stakes, guarantees, vendor support). Hyperscalers have more outgoing than incoming links, and chipmakers and frontier labs receive credit enhancements and equity financing. HSBC compares chipmaker vendor financing to Nortel and Lucent in 2001.

Residual value guarantees can be weakened by trigger conditions, lease termination rights after delays of about 180 days, and disputes over how residual value is measured. GPU depreciation schedules are highly uncertain and stranded asset risk exists if compute demand falls short.

Pricing power is unlikely to stay with semiconductors. ASICs such as Google's TPU and cheaper open-weight models could erode margins of GPU vendors and frontier labs. Historically most value from new technologies goes to end users. HSBC sees vertically integrated hyperscalers as the most resilient credit profiles.

Returns test: a Columbia Business School study, assuming 10% ROIC, puts the AI revenue needed to support current capex at USD2.8-5.5trn by 2032, against US software spending of about USD1.6trn in Q2 2026. These are illustrations, not forecasts.

US credit: neutral. Tactical overweight in hyperscaler bonds including 30y, and selected datacentre bonds. Hyperscaler spreads carry about a 75bp AI-related premium near the September peak. 1y forward free cashflow estimates fell about USD300bn in 2026, and HSBC thinks 2026 is the peak of capex growth.

US sector changes: Communications upgraded to Overweight from Neutral, Consumer Non-Cyclicals cut to Underweight from Overweight, Basic Industry cut to Underweight, Autos cut to Neutral from Overweight. Utilities and Technology stay Overweight, Energy stays Underweight. Communications spreads widened about 40bp vs US IG on the SpaceX spectrum competition fear, which HSBC thinks is overdone.

EUR credit: upgrade EUR IG and HY to mildly bullish. Upgrades to Overweight: Banks (incl. T2s), Real Estate, Autos, Hybrids. AT1 to Neutral from Underweight. Downgrade Food and Beverage and Consumer Non-Cyclicals to Underweight. Tactical overweight in French banks, which trade about 15-20bp wide of eurozone peers, with OAT spreads expected to stay above 100bp over Bunds.

EUR Autos trade about 30bp wide of EUR Industrials, near the top of the historic range. Auto hybrids offer about 200bp over senior bonds (over 300bp for STLA) against about 100bp for EUR hybrids on average. HSBC prefers short-call Auto hybrids to longer senior paper and says the case rests on positioning and valuation, not improving fundamentals.

GBP credit: neutral. Gilt yields rose over 100bp. GBP hyperscaler bonds at 10-15y yield about 6.5% with spreads of 150bp vs 5.8% and 67bp for GBP AA corporates. HSBC likes hyperscaler GBP bonds, Communications, and Utilities over Financials, and stays cautious on French and other bank bonds in GBP.

GCC credit: mildly bullish. The residual geopolitical premium is about 10bp, down from a 25-30bp peak in March. Overweight Bank T2s and pipeline bonds (KSA pipelines preferred over UAE), long-end UAE and Oman sovereigns. Neutral KSA, Kuwait and Bahrain, mildly bearish Qatar. GCC AT1s are too tight.

GCC issuance: USD issuance forecast to rise 23% to USD135-150bn. Sovereigns prefer private placements and local markets. Banks may fund offshore as loan-to-deposit ratios rise, and this issuance is the main risk to GCC spreads.

Asia credit: neutral. Asia USD supply forecast down 11% with negative net issuance again, since local currency funding is cheaper (CNH about 2.2% vs about 6% for USD IG). Overweight India, Macau, mainland China Internet and BBs. Underweight Indonesia (quasi-sovereigns carrying fuel subsidies, Danantara mandate uncertainty), Malaysia and Singapore.

Private credit is the main default vulnerability, not HY bonds. Private credit default rates are rising while HY and loan defaults moderate. A 2028 maturity wall looms, and software loans are a large part of private credit. In an S&P sample of 415 software firms, about 25% could benefit from AI and about a third are at risk of disruption.

Supply forecasts: hyperscalers about USD365bn in 2027 (USD270bn USD IG, EUR40bn EUR IG), USD IG non-financials USD1.1trn, EUR IG EUR795bn, GBP IG up about 11%, USD datacentre HY and unrated issuance USD60-90bn, hybrids USD50-60bn in the US and EUR45-55bn in Europe.

market_movers.rationale: Tactical overweight on hyperscaler bonds including 30y, as spreads carry about a 75bp AI premium and balance sheets can absorb AI cycle shocks. This covers the bonds of Microsoft, Alphabet, Meta, Amazon and Oracle.
US Communications upgraded to Overweight from Neutral after about 40bp of underperformance vs US IG. HSBC thinks the SpaceX competition risk is overpriced.
US Consumer Non-Cyclicals cut to Underweight after outperformance leaves less attractive risk-reward.
US Basic Industry cut to Underweight. Chemicals margin uplift from the Middle East conflict is priced in and spreads are near decade tights.
US Autos cut to Neutral from Overweight as the spread gap to Industrials narrowed from about 40-50bp to about 10bp.
EUR Autos upgraded to Overweight from Underweight on a roughly 30bp spread premium to Industrials and bearish positioning, not improving fundamentals.
EUR Banks (incl. T2s) and Real Estate upgraded to Overweight, with a tactical overweight in French banks on a 15-20bp spread premium.
EUR corporate hybrids upgraded to Overweight as the sub-senior spread differential nearly doubled from about 70bp to about 100bp.
EUR Food and Beverage cut to Underweight. It now trades inside the index, offers no carry and faces margin pressure.
US Utilities stay Overweight, backed by regulated earnings and PPAs with hyperscalers, with equity and hybrids used to fund capex.

sector_views.rationale: Regulated earnings and PPAs give stable cashflow and borrowing is constrained by existing leverage.
Upgraded after underperformance. Spread uplift of about 50bp vs Industrials and a steep curve, with incumbents having balance sheet room to defend share.
Unchanged. Hyperscalers favoured for resilience across AI scenarios.
Tight spreads limit further outperformance even if oil stays elevated.
Margin uplift from Middle East capacity curtailment is priced in.
Spread advantage over Industrials largely gone and sales expected to plateau.
Banks, T2s and Real Estate upgraded as political and rate risks are reflected in spreads.
Bearish sentiment overshot and spreads are about 30bp wide of Industrials.
Competitiveness challenges and energy costs weigh on the sector.
Trades inside the index with margin pressure from food prices and weak pricing power.
Utilities preferred over Financials, where sovereign spillover risk is underpriced.
Shorter duration, higher carry, resilient fundamentals and wide T2 valuations vs DM peers.
Spreads compensate for AI capex and cash buffers are substantial.
Quasi-sovereigns bear fuel subsidy costs and policy uncertainty around Danantara persists.

trade_ideas.description: Tactical overweight in USD hyperscaler bonds including 30y, an exception to the cautious stance on 30y IG
trade_ideas.rationale: Spreads carry a 75bp AI premium that can compress as supply uncertainty fades and capex growth peaks.
trade_ideas.risk: Supply-related spread pressure and AI return disappointment.

trade_ideas.description: Overweight selected datacentre bonds with NNN hyperscaler leases, amortisation within the lease term and modest construction risk
trade_ideas.rationale: 100-200bp spread uplift vs the tenant hyperscaler with duration inside 5y and contractual cashflows.
trade_ideas.risk: Tenant downgrade, construction delays and force majeure disputes.

trade_ideas.description: Overweight EUR BBs, T2s and corporate hybrids over spread duration
trade_ideas.rationale: Elevated yields mean attractive total returns without needing spread compression.
trade_ideas.risk: Disorderly OAT widening or fiscal spillover.

trade_ideas.description: Tactical overweight in French bank senior and sub credit
trade_ideas.rationale: Circa 15-20bp premium to eurozone peers with a domestic investor bid.
trade_ideas.risk: Escalating OAT volatility with spillover to other European banks. HSBC would revert to caution if the spread gap closes.

trade_ideas.description: Overweight short-call EUR Auto hybrids over longer senior Auto paper
trade_ideas.rationale: About 200bp spread over senior, more than 300bp for STLA.
trade_ideas.risk: Cyclical headwinds, raw material costs and rating pressure.

trade_ideas.description: Overweight GCC Bank T2s and pipeline bonds, with KSA pipelines preferred over UAE
trade_ideas.rationale: T2s trade wide vs DM peers. KSA pipeline bonds offer 50-70bp extra spread in the 5-10y range.
trade_ideas.risk: Heavier than expected bank and sovereign issuance and refinancing risk at Green Palm.

trade_ideas.description: Long 10y+ Oman and UAE sovereign bonds, neutral KSA, Kuwait and Bahrain, underweight Qatar
trade_ideas.rationale: 10y+ Oman and UAE trade about 120bp and 100bp wide to Treasuries vs about 90bp in US IG.

trade_ideas.description: Overweight GBP Utilities over Financials, plus GBP hyperscaler and Communications bonds
trade_ideas.rationale: GBP hyperscaler bonds at 150bp vs 67bp for GBP AA. Financials carry underpriced sovereign spillover risk.
trade_ideas.risk: Gilt volatility and UK fiscal or political shocks.

trade_ideas.description: Overweight India credit, China Internet and Asia BBs, underweight Indonesia quasi-sovereigns
trade_ideas.rationale: China Internet spreads have repriced for AI capex headwinds. Indonesia quasi-sovereigns carry fuel subsidy costs.
trade_ideas.risk: Higher than expected Chinese or Indian USD supply.

risk_factors: Weakening underwriting standards across datacentre and GPU-backed debt.
Leveraged AI pure plays such as neoclouds are most exposed in a halt scenario.
Corporates reliant on external capital: CCCs and private credit (direct lending), with a 2028 maturity wall.
Circular financing and a web of AI interdependencies (leases, guarantees, equity stakes) that makes portfolios less diversified than they look.
Residual value guarantees can be weakened by conditions, termination rights after delays and valuation disputes.
GPU depreciation uncertainty and stranded asset risk.
Datacentre construction delays, force majeure and grid or permitting constraints.
OAT spreads widening disorderly with fiscal and election-driven spillover to EUR and GBP spread markets.
Energy shock proving more entrenched, leading to a more hawkish ECB and Fed pricing and pressure on energy-importing Asian currencies such as the INR.
Issuance above expectations in GCC banks, Indian USD debt or Kuwait Petroleum's sale and leaseback financing.
Supply from new Communications entrants such as SpaceX eroding incumbent margins.
Pricing power leakage from semiconductors and frontier labs and ASIC competition vs GPUs.
charts_described: Figure B3 shows 12m long-run ex-post vs forward ex-ante Sharpe ratios, with USD IG, EUR IG, USD HY and EUR HY near the top at about 0.8 to 0.4.
Figure C1 shows the AI buildout (2025-2032) as a larger share of GDP than railroads, electrification, highways and telecoms booms.
Figure C3 shows 2027 gross issuance forecast of USD1,980bn against demand from redemptions, coupon reinvestments, ETFs, insurers and foreigners.
Figure C5 plots real yields vs government borrowing as a share of domestic savings, with higher savings associated with lower real yields.
Figure C16 shows rated datacentre debt force majeure risk counts of 53 low, 20 moderate, 24 elevated and 3 high.
Figure H1 shows GCC residual OAS change with a current geopolitical risk premium of 10bp vs a peak of 25-30bp.
vol_and_positioning: Hyperscaler spreads carry about a 75bp AI-related premium, near the September peak.
Hyperscaler and chip spreads have decoupled from and underperformed the rest of the AI credit complex.
Foreign investors, including Japan-based buyers, continue to buy US credit despite rising JGB yields.
Positioning and sentiment in EUR Autos has turned too bearish, with some forced unwinding among leveraged players seen in OAT spreads at the start of Q4 2026.
Communications spreads widened almost 40bp vs US IG while Consumer Non-Cyclicals tightened.
French banks trade 15-20bp wide of eurozone peers, with 10-15bp of carry to harvest if the status quo holds.
EUR hybrids sub-senior spread differential nearly doubled from about 70bp to about 100bp, and is about 200bp in Autos and over 300bp for STLA.
Datacentre bonds have held up well vs hyperscaler debt on a duration-adjusted basis over the past year.
geopolitical: The Middle East conflict and Strait of Hormuz flows, with HSBC's baseline of gradual but incomplete normalisation, keeping oil and gas prices higher.
Iran conflict unresolved, with a residual GCC geopolitical spread premium of about 10bp vs a 25-30bp peak in March.
Renewed conflict between the Houthis and Saudi Arabia hit project pipeline bond valuations.
East-West pipeline in Saudi Arabia and pipelines bypassing Hormuz as a theme for GCC borrowing.
Qatar LNG exports constrained by the Hormuz disruption.
French election and Rassemblement National's strong polling, plus elections in Italy, Spain and Greece and a possible early UK general election.
US midterm elections as a potential slowdown trigger for new datacentre construction.
Bahrain financial support from other GCC members and the AED20bn swap line from April 2026.
Oracle force majeure on Project Jupiter in New Mexico over regulatory delays on a gas pipeline connection.
Indonesia fuel subsidies and Danantara mandate expansion.
Chinese competition in autos and proposed caps on Chinese car imports to Europe.
El Niño and higher fertiliser prices pushing food inflation in Asia around Q2 2027.
cross_bank_references: Moody's expects Chinese hyperscalers to spend around USD165bn on capex in 2027, up from USD65bn in 2025.
Fitch has highlighted the possibility that Indonesia might lean on quasi-fiscal channels such as Danantara to meet its funding needs.
Columbia Business School study (Stijn Van Nieuwerburgh) estimates AI revenue of USD2.8-5.5trn by 2032 would be required at a 10% ROIC.
S&P expects US light vehicle sales to plateau in coming years.
Moody's expects SOE dividend payouts in Indonesia to stay elevated.

tension_points.bull_case: Borrowing continues with moderating growth, spreads stay in the 80-100bp range and carry delivers high-single-digit total returns. Hyperscalers have balance sheet capacity and capex growth peaks in 2026.
tension_points.bear_case: Markets could question AI returns. Annual AI revenue of USD2.8-5.5trn by 2032 would be needed, and a halt would push IG spreads beyond 120bp and hit leveraged neoclouds hardest.
tension_points.what_invalidates: IG spreads widening above 120bp as markets lose confidence in AI returns, or earnings and ROIC failing to catch up with the liabilities being created.

tension_points.bull_case: Spreads carry a 75bp AI premium that can compress as supply uncertainty fades and capex growth decelerates, and off-balance-sheet structures ease IG indigestion.
tension_points.bear_case: Pace of issuance (USD25bn deals) pressures secondary spreads and a very large 2027 borrowing programme could keep the premium elevated.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Another USD300bn-sized fall in consensus forward free cashflow estimates in 2027 or a renewed surge in supply.

tension_points.bull_case: Spreads widened about 40bp, offer a roughly 50bp premium to Industrials and the curve can flatten as incumbents with spectrum, networks and balance sheets defend share.
tension_points.bear_case: A fourth entrant takes share mechanically and erodes incumbent margins, and further spectrum or capex progress by SpaceX would hurt incumbents.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Further spectrum acquisition or significant infrastructure capex by SpaceX that is perceived as credible.

tension_points.bull_case: Banks trade 15-20bp wide of peers with a domestic bid, so any positive budget or political surprise compresses the premium and carry is 10-15bp otherwise.
tension_points.bear_case: A disorderly OAT widening could spill over to other European sovereigns and bank spreads, and the French election raises scrutiny.
tension_points.what_invalidates: The spread gap to eurozone peers closing, at which point HSBC reverts to a cautious stance as in June 2026 when the gap was zero.

theme_stances.key_argument: Spreads have already widened and now compensate for macro and political risks, favouring BBs, T2s and hybrids.
